title: Pluralistic evaluation harness for low-precision task scoring and calibration regression gating
creator: Ava Morgan
description: Background: As we onboard FP8 and INT8 quantization profiles, teams have requested a single, extensible evaluation harness that (1) computes task-specific accuracy metrics, (2) produces distributional and uncertainty-aware signals for gating, and (3) integrates with existing calibration workflows and the Console regression gate. Scope: implement a 'pluralistic' metric layer that runs multiple scorers per workload (perplexity, MMLU-style exam suites, Rouge/BLEU for summarization, token-level F1 for NER, exact-match + EM-fallback for QA, code exec pass@1 for code tasks), adds seed/stability and sample-variance bands, and emits a compact metric contract used by rollouts. Key goals: - Canonical scorer interfaces (metric name, task type, input mapping, reference lookup) - Pluggable adapters so teams can add task-specific scorers without runtime changes - Per-metric confidence intervals (bootstrap-based) and delta-to-baseline with p-values - Produce a single gating payload (json-line) that Console and the calibration orchestrator can consume - Link metrics to quant profile metadata (quant config id, calibration snapshot id, kernel/exec platform) Acceptance criteria: - The harness can run on our evaluation infra and produce results for at least 6 canonical tasks within CI (LM perplexity, MMLU 4-shot sim, summarization Rouge-L, translation BLEU, NER F1, code pass@1) - Each metric includes CI at 95%% and a delta-vs-baseline field - A gating decision enum is emitted: {PASS, WARN, FAIL} with rule provenance - Integration test in runtime-1.22 that wires the gating payload into canary rollouts - Console shows a per-metric time series and a single 'low-precision gate' indicator Design notes: - Scorers implement a simple contract: input_transform (python), score(batch_predictions, references) -> {value: float, sample_values: [floats], details: string}. We'll serialize contract metadata as json-lines to avoid nested objects in downstream sinks. - CI for small datasets uses stratified bootstrapping (1000 resamples) to produce 95%% CI; large datasets use approximate methods (jackknife/Poisson sampling) for throughput - Metric aggregation: when tasks run multiple sub-metrics (e.g., Rouge-{1,2,L}), we compute a task-level composite via weighted harmonic mean; weights configured per project via a yaml file stored in repo - Confidence-aware gating rules: by default FAIL if primary metric delta < -0.5%% AND p-value < 0.01; WARN if delta between -0.5%% and -0.1%%, or instability (std/sqrt(n) > threshold) - Telemetry: emit per-run artifacts to S3 evaluations bucket and a lightweight summary to the metrics-warehouse (consistent schema). Implementation plan: 1) Metric SDK: python package with scorer base class + built-in scorers (perplexity, rouge, bleu, mmlu-adapter, ner-f1, code-exec harness) 2) CI runner: reuse eval workers; add bootstrap step as optional stage 3) Calibration hook: runner writes calibration_snapshot_id and quant_profile_id into metrics payload 4) Console ingestion: new parser to visualize sample distributions and gate output 5) Regression rules: implement plugin in rollout controller to consume gating enum and block canaries if FAIL Datasets and tooling: - Use existing eval corpora (MMLU converted to internal format, GLUE-like suites for NER, WMT subset for BLEU, CNN/DM for Rouge) - Provide seed files and deterministic prompt templates to reduce brittle variance - Create a short 'sanity' dataset (100 examples per task) to run fast checks in PRs Rollout plan: - Phase 1: internal-only harness runs on CI for every quant-profile PR - Phase 2: wire harness into Dedicated calibration flows and write gating payload to canary runs - Phase 3: surface results in Console and enable optional auto-blocking for enterprise customers Open questions: - Should the metric SDK implement GPU-accelerated tokenization for throughput? (Trade-off: complexity vs speed) - Standardize on a single p-value method (bootstrap vs permutation) - How to version metric contracts so older Console backfills remain interpretable Artifacts & links: - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Q/Pluralistic+Metric+Layer (placeholder) - Initial PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-eval/pull/149 (placeholder) - Dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/quant/low-precision-harness (placeholder)
